headline: GOLDMAN SACHS TELLS INVESTORS: HOLD GOLD THROUGH DECEMBER — Two Forecast Cuts Later, Central Bank Demand Still Underpins Long-Term Thesis
snippet: TipRanks breaks down Goldman Sachs' current gold and silver outlook following two price-target cuts this month: GS lowered end-2026 gold to $4,150/oz and then made a second downgrade that turned its own bear case into the base case, citing rising Fed rate-hike expectations. Goldman still sees roughly 15–16% upside by end-2027 underpinned by central bank purchases running near 60 tonnes/month — a structural demand floor that the bank argues survives even a December rate hike. For retail investors deciding whether to hold or exit gold positions heading into the FOMC minutes release today and the December 9 policy decision, the analysis provides GS's reasoning for staying long at current levels while expecting continued near-term pressure.

headline: CHALICE DRILLS 15m AT 8.6 g/t GOLD, 2m AT 56.7 g/t AT KESTREL — High-Grade Copper-Gold System Opens 140km Western Extension of Tennant Creek Province
snippet: Chalice Mining (ASX: CHN) reported a standout intersection of 15 metres at 8.6 g/t gold and 0.54% copper from 78m depth at the Kestrel target within its Warrego North project — including a 2m section returning 56.7 g/t gold — confirming a new high-grade copper-gold discovery near the historic Warrego mine in the Northern Territory's Tennant Creek Mineral Field. The company is now expanding its tenure over what it interprets as a potential 140km western geological extension of the Tennant Creek province, with the approximately 1km gap between the Chook and Kestrel targets identified as a priority for step-out drilling. For junior mining investors, Tennant Creek geology has produced some of Australia's highest-grade gold deposits historically — a 15m at 8.6 g/t gold intercept in this setting is a first-pass result that warrants close attention.

headline: FED MINUTES DROP TODAY — Gold Bear Watch Key $3,650 Support; Any Dovish Signal Could Trigger Short-Covering Rally
snippet: FXEmpire's November 19 gold and silver price forecast identifies today's FOMC minutes release as the definitive near-term catalyst for the precious metals market, with gold's selloff having deepened through multiple technical support levels as markets price a December rate hike at approximately 92% probability. The analysis flags key support at $3,650 — a break of which would open a move toward the $3,500 zone — while noting that any hint of a less hawkish path in the minutes could trigger significant short-covering among leveraged Comex positions. Silver's lower support thresholds and higher volatility make it an asymmetric trade in either direction from current levels. For investors watching from the sidelines, the analysis frames today's minutes as a potential inflection point in the near-term directional narrative for both metals.

headline: NEEDHAM INITIATES MP MATERIALS WITH $48 BUY TARGET — Analyst Sees 25%+ Upside; Rare Earth Stock Rises 3.8% Amid Sector Volatility
snippet: Needham initiated coverage of MP Materials (NYSE: MP) with a Buy rating and $48 price target on November 18, sending shares up 3.8% in a session where most rare earth equities had been under pressure. The initiation comes the same day rare earth stocks staged a broad recovery on US-China trade talk optimism at APEC — suggesting growing analyst conviction in the sector at or near what may be technical lows. Needham's $48 target implies roughly 25% upside from pre-initiation prices. For investors evaluating entry points in the rare earth space, a first-time Buy initiation from a growth-focused tech and materials investment bank at a 52-week low is a signal worth tracking — particularly in a week when the January 2027 China export control deadline is concentrating sector attention.

headline: SILVER FALLS BELOW 1980'S HUNT BROTHERS HIGH — Nominal $49.45 Breached as Metal Now Down 63% From Its January Record
snippet: Silver's selloff has crossed a threshold that separates this correction from every other drawdown of the past four decades: the metal has fallen below the nominal price of the January 1980 Hunt Brothers peak of approximately $49.45 per ounce — a level it has held above continuously since the 1980s. Down approximately 63% from its January 2026 record high of $121.60, silver is now trading at prices last seen before the commodity supercycle of the early 2000s, raising the question of whether this is a generational re-entry opportunity or a signal of structural demand headwinds. The article contextualizes the 1980 comparison against today's supply deficit and industrial demand backdrop.

headline: SQM QUARTERLY PROFIT HITS TWO-YEAR HIGH — Lithium Miner Beats Expectations the Same Week Citi Slashed Its Price Forecast 40%
snippet: SQM's quarterly profit reached its highest level in two years according to SMM Metal Market's analysis, driven by record lithium sales volumes and improving lithium prices — a result that arrives in direct contrast to Citigroup's this-week decision to cut its lithium price forecast by 40% to $12,000/t. The divergence between SQM's actual financial performance and Citi's structural bearishness illustrates the tension at the core of the lithium market: volume growth is delivering real earnings momentum even as the long-run price ceiling is being revised lower. For junior lithium developers tracking project economics, SQM's strong volumes alongside a Citi-endorsed $12,000/t floor create a bifurcated picture of near-term producer success versus longer-term development-stage risk.

headline: SCORPION MINERALS SIGNS BINDING DEAL FOR PAYNES FIND GOLD — 289 sq km Western Australia Project Changes Hands on November 19
snippet: Scorpion Minerals (ASX: SCN) announced a binding agreement to acquire 100% of the Paynes Find Gold Project covering 289 square kilometres in Western Australia on November 19, adding a significant gold land package in the Murchison Province to its existing exploration portfolio. The Paynes Find district has a heritage of gold production and sits in a region that has seen renewed exploration interest as the gold price — even at current 52-week lows — remains historically high for project economics. Junior M&A activity during gold price selloffs has historically preceded re-rating cycles for acquirers positioned to advance assets before the next leg up.

headline: RESOURO ADVANCES NOVO MUNDO TO TRIAL MINING — TSX-V Junior Mobilizes Equipment to Mato Grosso Gold Project in Brazil
snippet: Resouro Strategic Metals (TSX-V: RSM) has mobilized mining equipment to its Novo Mundo gold project in Mato Grosso, Brazil, moving the asset from exploration into trial mining — the operational stage that tests the economics of bulk-sample processing and provides early cash flow data. For junior mining investors, the transition from exploration to trial mining is a material de-risking event that transforms a project from a resource estimate into a revenue-generating test operation. Mato Grosso's established gold mining infrastructure and Brazil's improving regulatory environment for small-scale operators make Novo Mundo a relatively lower-risk jurisdiction for this next phase.

headline: UR-ENERGY TARGETS US URANIUM PRODUCTION LEADERSHIP — Shirley Basin Commissioning Advances as 120-Hole Lost Creek South Drill Runs
snippet: Crux Investor profiles Ur-Energy's (NYSE: URG) strategic positioning as the company moves simultaneously toward commissioning its Shirley Basin ISR uranium project in Wyoming and running a 120-hole (~84,000 ft.) exploration drill program at Lost Creek South. With Q3 2026 results showing a 67% year-over-year increase in uranium sales and 26% growth in captured pounds, Ur-Energy is demonstrating operational ramp-up at a time when uranium equities broadly trade near multi-year lows despite spot uranium above $90/lb. The piece argues that companies combining active production with organic exploration drilling have historically outperformed peers during uranium equity recoveries — a framework relevant to positioning in a sector where the URNM ETF trades 31% below its year-start level.

headline: ASX JUNIOR MINERS DEFYING THE 2026 SELLOFF — Stockhead Identifies Explorers Outperforming a 30-40% Sector Decline
snippet: Stockhead Australia's analysis identifies a cohort of ASX-listed junior exploration companies that have outperformed the broader gold and mining sector during the 2026 bear market, which has seen the GDXJ and comparable junior indices fall 30–40% from their August peaks. The common factors among outperformers include active 2026 drill programs with high-grade results, secured financing at the start of the year, and exposure to gold rather than lithium or base metals. The analysis serves as a framework for TSX-V and ASX investors trying to identify which names have the asset quality and balance sheet to emerge as consolidation targets or sector leaders when the macro headwinds recede.
